title: Tries
summary: A trie stores words letter by letter, so words with a shared prefix share a path. Insert and prefix lookup cost one step per letter, however many words are stored.
idea: Each edge is one letter and each node is a prefix. Mark the nodes where a word ends, and count how many words pass through each node.

signals.see: You must answer many questions about prefixes: starts-with, autocomplete or how many words begin with something.
signals.think: Build a trie once. Each query walks one node per letter of the prefix, whatever the dictionary size.

signals.see: You must find the shortest or longest stored word that is a prefix of some text.
signals.think: Walk the text through the trie letter by letter and note each end-of-word mark you pass.

signals.see: A grid or board search must check many dictionary words at once.
signals.think: Walk the trie alongside the search, and prune a path as soon as no word starts with it.

phrasings: A search box shows how many saved contacts start with the letters typed so far.
Replace each word in a sentence with the shortest dictionary stem it begins with.
Given a list of commands, find the longest prefix that they all share.

picture.title: Walk the prefix once
picture.alt: On the left, every stored word is compared with the prefix, so each query costs the number of words times the prefix length. On the right, the prefix is walked down a trie one letter at a time, and the count stored on the last node answers the query.
picture.caption: A prefix query costs one step per letter, not one check per word.

examples.label: A word is a prefix of another

visualiser.inputHelp: Words: 2 to 5 words of up to 5 lowercase letters, separated by commas or spaces. Prefix: one group of 1 to 5 lowercase letters.

oneLiner: insert: walk letters, create missing children, count++, mark end; query: walk the prefix or fail

exercise.prompt: roots is a list of word stems and sentence is lowercase words separated by single spaces. Replace every word that starts with a stem by the shortest such stem, and keep other words as they are. Return the new sentence. The starter keeps walking after it finds a stem, so it uses the longest stem instead of the shortest.

args: the cattle was rattled by the battery
tests.expected: the cat was rat by the bat

hints: Insert every stem into a trie and mark the node where each stem ends.
Walk each word through the trie. Return as soon as you reach an end mark, because that is the shortest stem. Keep the word if you fall off the trie.

complexity.why: Insert and lookup take one step per letter of the word or prefix, so O(L). In the worst case the trie stores one node for every letter of every word, when no prefixes are shared.

mistakes: Forgetting the end-of-word mark, so a stored prefix like “car” looks like a word when only “cart” was added.
Treating “no child for this letter” as “found”. It means no stored word has this prefix.
Scanning the whole trie to answer a count query instead of storing a count on each node during insert.
Creating new child nodes during a lookup, which silently adds prefixes to the trie.

quiz.question: You store “car” and “cart”. Which flag tells you “car” is a word and not only a prefix?
choices: The node for “r” has a child
The node for “r” is marked as the end of a word
The root has a child for “c”
quiz.explain: Shared paths are prefixes. Only the end mark says a whole word stops at that node.

quiz.question: How long does it take to check a prefix of length L in a trie holding n words?
quiz.explain: The walk takes one step per letter, whatever the number of stored words.

quiz.question: You must count words that start with a prefix, many times. What should each node store?
choices: The full list of words below it
How many inserted words pass through it
quiz.explain: Add 1 to every node on the path during insert. A count query then reads one number at the prefix's node.

interviewTip: Draw three words with a shared prefix as a small trie before coding. It makes the end-of-word mark and the per-node count obvious to you and the interviewer.
